topic.title: Tufa Labs’ Winning Solution for ARC-AGI-3 Milestone 1

comments.content: Thank you, this information is useful. Judging by the gradient table, this method is practically independent of the level complexity. The model is either able to find a pattern, or it isn't. To verify, you could run this test with another local model, for example, the one recently published in notebook: https://www.kaggle.com/code/gregkamradt/arc-agi-3-gpt-oss-120b. Within the competition, this will cost you practically nothing, but it will show how dependent the method is on the model's power.
Just finished reading this and its so cool to see you guys turned the game into code. I didn't think of that! Great write up as always! Thank you for the high effort and quality into this!
I think this represents the true spirit of a milestone prize. You are all clearly dedicated to advancing these domains and helping others do the same. Thank you!
Thank a lot! I really enjoy reading you. I learn a lot from you write up. Amazing contribution to humanity.
we have scored 9.76 on public train set will submit soon

We'd like to build on the duck harness per your invitation in the blog post, could you confirm its license or add a LICENSE file to the repo/notebook? The competition rules require third-party components to carry an explicit open-source license, so a one-line MIT-0/CC0 confirmation would let everyone building on your work stay prize-eligible
Hey, the licenses are included in the metadata of the kernel and notebook. The notebook is under Apache 2.0 license (the only one possible on Kaggle), the underlying code dataset on MIT license.

congrats on the score!!

have u guys tried integrating this pipeline with claude/gpt5?
Yes, but due to cost we've only done a few games. See here: https://tufalabs.ai/research/duck-harness
Thanks for this detailed explanation. It really helps to comprehend your solution and iterate it further.
